attempts.input: Project file names for odd project names. Typed each name into #project-name, then clicked 'Download the project file': '   ', '....', '../../etc/passwd', 'CON', 'nul', '日本の歯医者', '🎨🎨', '‮exe.txt', 'a'×120, 'Ψ project', and in a fresh page 'Ünïcödé Ltd.'.
attempts.observed: '   ', '....', '日本の歯医者', '🎨🎨' and 'Ψ project' all became 'project.refraction.json'. Every name in a script without Latin letters gets that same generic name, so different projects collide. 'Ünïcödé Ltd.' became 'u-ni-co-de-ltd.refraction.json': NFKD splits each accented letter into a letter plus a mark, and the mark is replaced by a hyphen. 'Müller' would come out as 'mu-ller'. 'CON' became 'con.refraction.json' and 'nul' became 'nul.refraction.json', which are device names on Windows. '../../etc/passwd' became 'etc-passwd.refraction.json' (no path escape). The RTL mark was stripped ('exe-txt.refraction.json'). 120 a's were cut to 40. The name inside each file always matched the screen. Severity: names are misleading but not dangerous.

attempts.input: Clicked 'Download the project file' 14 times in a row on one Summary page (Chromium, file:// page).
attempts.observed: Downloads 1–10 and 12–14 arrived. Download #11 never arrived: no download event within 4 s, and the same thing happened at the 11th download in a2_full.cjs. Each time the message still read 'The project file “plain.refraction.json” was handed to your browser to save, usually into your Downloads folder…'. The text is identical to the previous one, so nothing tells the owner that this click produced no file. saveFile returns 'saved' as soon as link.click() runs (platform.ts:483-491), whatever the browser does next. Caveat: the drop is probably Chromium's own limit on repeated downloads, not the Studio, but the message claims a hand-over that produced no file.

attempts.input: Kept copy whose text holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate. Seeded entry 'refraction.project.backup.<time>.seedlone' with text '{"name":"half \uD83D emoji"}', then 'Download this kept copy'. Other seeded texts: CRLF, BOM, NUL, plain words.
attempts.observed: The lone-surrogate copy downloaded as 'refraction-kept-copy-3.json' holding '{"name":"half � emoji"}': the Blob's UTF-8 encoding replaced the surrogate with U+FFFD, so the file is not the kept text character for character. The CRLF, BOM, NUL and plain-word copies were exact. A copy that starts with a BOM but is JSON downloads as '.txt', because JSON.parse rejects the BOM. This needs hand-made or hostile storage; the Studio's own writes escape lone surrogates.
